cluster.title: The golden opportunity for American AI
cluster.description: A golden opportunity lies ahead for America to harness the transformative power of AI—today’s electricity—to revolutionize the economy, secure global leadership, and build a foundation for prosperity through innovation, skilling, and international collaboration.

extra_snippets: And it includes FinOps, too. As AI scales, every organization needs a clear line between what it spends and the value AI creates. That is why today we are announcing Agent 365 Business Analytics. You can think of it as your ERP system for AI usage. You can see exactly what is driving spend.

The next thing I want to talk about is how you take the environment you have set up, from Copilot to IQ to Agent 365, and secure it. And that is where Perception and our security stack comes in. We are building an end-to-end trust platform. We are helping customers both secure their AI deployments and use AI to strengthen their security posture.

But we cannot see what happens inside the model. And what the model tells us about itself is not independent evidence. These nested black boxes are simply unacceptable. We need to be able to examine what AI sees and does, verify its actions independently and control what it is allowed to do.

There are three parts to this: First, we will expand our collaboration in NIST’s Agent Standards Initiative, drawing on its research to help lead the development of open, industry-wide standards for AI transparency, security and governance.

results.title: Security fundamentals to enable the frontier - Microsoft On the Issues
results.description: A few weeks ago, Microsoft revealed that Storm-0940, a China-aligned hacking group, used an AI framework to attack hundreds of organizations at once, in some cases obtaining privileged cloud access in under three hours.

meta_url.path: › home  › security fundamentals to enable the frontier

extra_snippets: As AI accelerates cyber threats, organizations must strengthen cybersecurity fundamentals, address tech debt, close patching gaps, and secure AI agents.

This summer gave us a preview of the next era of cyber conflict. Frontier AI models under evaluation slipped their controls and broke into external systems they were never authorized to access. More concerning, in many cases, developers discovered these incidents only weeks or even months later.

Breakthrough AI was only part of the story. Each incident exploited the oldest weaknesses in computing: too much access, too little visibility, and patches that arrived too late. Old failures at machine speed. AI doesn’t replace the fundamentals.

A few weeks ago, Microsoft revealed that Storm-0940, a China-aligned hacking group, used an AI framework to attack hundreds of organizations at once, in some cases obtaining privileged cloud access in under three hours.
